meta.location: Desolation, Teancum, Boaz, and the hill Shim
principles: A judgment carried out by other wicked men
A record keeper who steps back in

world_behind.title: Mormon is not leading
world_behind.text: He resigned in Mormon 3:11 and narrates this chapter from outside command.

world_behind.title: The aggression is named as the cause
world_behind.text: Without the Nephite advance, verse 4 says, the enemy would have held no power at all.

world_behind.title: The mechanism of judgment is stated
world_behind.text: Verse 5 makes one set of wicked men the instrument for punishing another.

world_behind.title: Boasting recurs
world_behind.text: Verse 8 repeats the pattern from Mormon 3:9.

world_behind.title: Prisoners are sacrificed
world_behind.text: Verses 14 and 21 both report Nephite women and children offered as sacrifices to idol gods. Nothing else in the volume reports human sacrifice by either nation, and Moroni 9:8 to 10 gives the only comparable atrocity, in a private letter rather than the history.

world_behind.title: A superlative is recorded
world_behind.text: Verse 12 sets this wickedness above anything among the children of Lehi or the house of Israel. Jacob 3:5 and Helaman 6:1 had both made the reverse comparison at earlier points, rating the Lamanites more righteous; the scale is used in both directions across the record.

world_behind.title: He acts again at the end
world_behind.text: Verse 23 has him go to the hill Shim and take up all the records.

words.text: Driven back. The record uses the word twice, here and at Alma 51:31, and the King James Bible not at all. Verse 8 has the Lamanites driven off Teancum.
Kept on despite everything. Its count is one, here, while the King James Bible has none. Verse 10 uses it of their wickedness.
Took pleasure in. The record uses the word six times and the King James Bible twelve. Verse 11 attaches it to the shedding of blood.
An image worshipped as a god. The word turns up twice, here and again at 1 Nephi 20:5, here, and the King James Bible sixteen times. Verse 14 has prisoners offered to idol gods.
Moisture that settles overnight and burns off. The record uses the word once, here, and the King James Bible thirty-seven times. Verse 18 uses it for how fast the Nephites are swept away.
Killing on a large scale. Treated at Mosiah 10:20. Its count is eighteen times in this book, while the King James Bible fifty-six.
Small settlements. The word runs to six here, twice in this book, against seventy-five in the King James Bible. Verse 22 says the flight emptied both towns and villages.

phrases.term: It was because the armies of the Nephites went up unto the Lamanites that they began to be smitten
phrases.text: The cause given plainly. Verse 4 says the Lamanites could have had no power over them otherwise.

phrases.term: It is by the wicked that the wicked are punished
phrases.text: The chapter's rule for how judgment arrives. No divine intervention is described; other men do it.

phrases.term: They did again boast of their own strength
phrases.text: The same reaction to the same kind of win. Mormon 3:9 had recorded it before the oath.

phrases.term: The Nephites repented not of the evil they had done, but persisted
phrases.text: Repentance ruled out after a fresh attack. The verse uses a word found nowhere else in the record.

phrases.term: Impossible for the tongue to describe, or for man to write a perfect description
phrases.text: The limit of the account. He says what he cannot put down and then sums it in one clause.

phrases.term: Every heart was hardened, so that they delighted in the shedding of blood
phrases.text: Hardness described as pleasure. The line covers both peoples.

phrases.term: There never had been so great wickedness among all the children of Lehi
phrases.text: A superlative, extended in the same verse to all the house of Israel. He attributes the measure to the words of the Lord.

phrases.term: Did offer them up as sacrifices unto their idol gods
phrases.text: The practice reported twice, here and at verse 21. Both times the prisoners are women and children.

phrases.term: Swept off by them even as a dew before the sun
phrases.text: The image for the rest of the book. What follows is the speed of it.

phrases.term: They did stand against the Lamanites with exceeding boldness
phrases.text: One line of credit in a chapter of collapse. It holds only until the second attack.

phrases.term: I did go to the hill Shim, and did take up all the records
phrases.text: Mormon acting on his own again. The charge from Mormon 1:3 is what he returns to.

verses.label: v. 1–3
verses.title: Two city names tracked through five reversals
verses.text: The record follows Desolation and Teancum by name rather than by campaign. Desolation is lost at verse 2, retaken at verse 8, and lost again at verse 13. Teancum receives the refugees at verse 3, is attacked and holds at verses 7 and 8, and falls at verse 14. Six changes of possession across two names in fourteen verses, each one dated to a year of the judges. The chapter is structured as a ledger of two places, and the fighting is reported only insofar as it moves them from one column to the other.

verses.label: v. 5
verses.title: A maxim dropped into a chronicle
verses.text: The record breaks off the narrative for a single sentence of general theory: "it is by the wicked that the wicked are punished; for it is the wicked that stir up the hearts of the children of men unto bloodshed." No names, no dates, no places. It is the only such statement in the chapter, and it stands between a defeat and the preparations for the next battle. The compiler is explaining the mechanism by which the judgments of the previous clause actually arrive.

verses.label: v. 11–12
verses.title: A refusal to describe, followed by a superlative claim
verses.text: The record states its own limit twice over inside verse 11: "impossible for the tongue to describe, or for man to write a perfect description of the horrible scene." Then, having said the thing cannot be described, it makes a comparative claim about it that reaches past its own people: "there never had been so great wickedness among all the children of Lehi, nor even among all the house of Israel." The claim is attributed, "according to the words of the Lord," so the record declines to measure the scene and reports a measurement of it in the same breath.

verses.label: v. 23
verses.title: The archive moved, in the first person
verses.text: The chapter ends with the compiler acting rather than reporting: "I, Mormon, seeing that the Lamanites were about to overthrow the land, therefore I did go to the hill Shim, and did take up all the records which Ammaron had hid up unto the Lord." This is the errand assigned at Mormon 1:3, executed here under military pressure. The verse gives no battle and no date, only a man retrieving a library, and it is the last thing recorded before the account resumes at Mormon 5.

chapter.title: The fall is dated to a decision
chapter.text: Verse 4 traces it to the Nephites going up. The chapter names an act rather than a mood.

chapter.title: Judgment works through other people
chapter.text: Verse 5 says the wicked punish the wicked. The mechanism is left entirely human.

chapter.title: The same error repeats
chapter.text: Verse 8 has them boast again after a win, exactly as in Mormon 3:9. Nothing was learned from the first time.

chapter.title: The record marks its own inadequacy
chapter.text: Verse 11 says no man can write a perfect description. He gives the summary and stops.

chapter.title: Delight is the diagnosis
chapter.text: Verse 11 says they delighted in bloodshed. The problem has moved past anger.

chapter.title: The atrocity is reported twice without comment
chapter.text: Verses 14 and 21 both record women and children sacrificed. Mormon adds no interpretation either time.

chapter.title: A single image carries the rest of the book
chapter.text: Verse 18 gives the dew before the sun. Everything after is that sentence working out.

chapter.title: He re-enters as a record keeper
chapter.text: Verse 23 has him retrieve the plates while refusing the army. The book he is making outlasts the war he will not lead.

applications.title: Count the cost of going on the attack
applications.text: The verse says the aggression is what gave the enemy power. Some losses begin with a choice to escalate.

applications.title: Do not read other people's cruelty as your vindication
applications.text: The wicked punish the wicked. Being on the receiving end is not proof of innocence.

applications.title: Notice the second boast
applications.text: The same reaction to the same win, one chapter later. Patterns you have already been warned about are the easiest to repeat.

applications.title: Say when you cannot describe it
applications.text: Mormon writes that no tongue could describe and no man write a perfect description of what he watched. Stating the limit of your account is more accurate than attempting the description and falling short of it.

applications.title: Anger can win a battle and settle nothing
applications.text: The Nephites, angry that their women and children had been sacrificed, beat the Lamanites and drove them from their lands, and the war went on. Rage is usable fuel for one engagement and has never once been a plan.

applications.title: Mark where the trend changed
applications.text: From this point the Nephites gained no power at all, and the record fixes the moment: swept off as a dew before the sun. Identifying the exact place a decline became irreversible is work only a later reader can do, and it is worth doing.

applications.title: Take everybody with you
applications.text: When they fled again they took all the inhabitants with them, from the towns and from the villages both. A retreat that carries people and one that leaves them are different events, and which one you get is decided beforehand.

applications.title: Save what will outlast the crisis
applications.text: He went for the records while the land was falling. Deciding early what must survive is its own kind of work.

questions.text: What trouble of mine started when I went on the offensive?
Where have I been an instrument of someone else's judgment?
What win made me forget who gave it?
What have I persisted in after being shown the cost?
What have I grown to take pleasure in that I should not?
What is being swept off faster than I expected?
If the land were falling, what would I go back for?

entries.reason: the records he later hides again at Cumorah

targets.quote: hid up in the hill Cumorah all the records which had been entrusted to me
targets.verse_text: And it came to pass that when we had gathered in all our people in one to the land of Cumorah, behold I, Mormon, began to be old; and knowing it to be the last struggle of my people, and having been commanded of the Lord that I should not suffer the records which had been handed down by our fathers, which were sacred, to fall into the hands of the Lamanites, (for the Lamanites would destroy them) therefore I made this record out of the plates of Nephi, and hid up in the hill Cumorah all the records which had been entrusted to me by the hand of the Lord, save it were these few plates which I gave unto my son Moroni.
targets.markdown: And it came to pass that when we had gathered in all our people in one to the land of Cumorah, behold I, Mormon, began to be old; and knowing it to be the last struggle of my people, and having been commanded of the Lord that I should not suffer the records which had been handed down by our fathers, which were sacred, to fall into the hands of the Lamanites, (for the Lamanites would destroy them) therefore I made this record out of the plates of Nephi, and **hid up in the hill Cumorah all the records which had been entrusted to me** by the hand of the Lord, save it were these few plates which I gave unto my son Moroni.
